items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Macky Kasper, whom I had jammed with in West Berlin 6 months before.

ctx.x: As this was my first time in Berlin, Hans and Fritz took me out sight-seeing the 30th. The effects of the bombings that Berlin suffered in World War II could be seen everywhere, but the bricks from the ruins were stacked in neat piles and the streets were the cleanest I've ever seen anywhere. I saw the gateway to East Berlin, the Russian war memorial and the stadium where Hitler had refused to shake hands with the great American Negro athlete Jessie Owens during the 1936 Olympic Games.

I did my second concert in a different theatre from the first one and in a different part of the city. There was a German trumpetist on the bill that night who was known as the best jazz trumpeter in Germany. His name was Macky Kasper and he was good. But his main claim to fame was that he could blow loud. He had some "iron chops" as we say in musical terms for a trumpeter. After the concert I went back to the club I had visited the night before and jammed with the cats again. Tiger Jones was also on the scene.…

In April I did concerts and balls in France and Belgium. The 7th I was coming back when Lily and Jimmy Davis met me at the railroad station. Jimmy told me that he was engaged to do a cabaret scene in a movie being filmed called 'The Respectful Prostitute', from a Jean-Paul Sartre novel. Joe Benjamin, the bass man and Bill Clark a drummer, were in France with Lena Horne, and they were going to make this cabaret scene also. Aaron Bridges was the pianist.
